object: graffito of three lines of very early characters, scratched on the right jamb of a temple door
site: Wadi Halfa (Buhen), left bank below the Second Cataract, the southern of the two Egyptian temples of Horus of Buhen
notes: Copy from the original checked with a small photograph by Blackman; Pl. VII. Griffith prints the three stone lines as one type line, without line numbers. On the left is a vertical line and a numeral probably reading 3,400, 6,400 or 9,400, resembling Egyptian hieratic (not printed in type; he doubts it belongs to the inscription). Griffith's '?' stands at the upper left of the second to-sign. On p. 26 he compares treN here with trens 'of tren' in no. 92, l. 2.
